findings.body:
The early return for empty input was removed. For an empty slice, `samples.iter().sum()` is 0 and `samples.len() as u32` is 0, so `total / 0` is evaluated. Integer division by zero panics in every build profile, while the doc comment on line 1 promises 0. `report` calls `average` directly, so an empty input reaches the panic.

Trigger: Calling `average(&[])` or `report(&[])`, for example a report over zero samples.

Impact: Any caller passing an empty slice, including `report(&[])`, panics with a division-by-zero instead of returning 0. This breaks the documented contract and can crash the caller.
findings.suggestion: Restore the `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` guard before the division.
findings.title: average panics with division by zero on empty input

findings.body:
The diff removes the `samples.is_empty()` guard that returned 0. For an empty slice, `total` is 0 and `samples.len() as u32` is 0, so the division `total / samples.len() as u32` divides by zero and panics. `report` calls `average` unconditionally, so it panics too.

Trigger: Calling average(&[]) or report(&[]), for example with a sample set that has no entries yet.

Impact: Any caller of `average` or `report` with an empty slice now panics instead of getting 0 as the doc comment promises. This is a regression from the old behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Restore the early return: `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` before the sum.
findings.title: average panics on empty input after removing the zero-length guard
